Failure modes such as erosion, cracking, spalling, blockage, leakage, and insufficient pressure or cooling are common and can be caused by high temperature, thermal shock, mechanical stress, wear and tear, corrosion, or mechanical failure. The severity of these failures ranges from reduced efficiency to complete shutdown, and their detectability varies, with some failures being easily detectable through regular inspections and others requiring advanced diagnostic tools. To prevent these failures, it is crucial to implement regular maintenance, monitoring, and inspection programs, addressing issues such as buildup of material, wear and tear, and mechanical failure before they escalate. Understanding the failure modes, reasons, codes, degradation mechanisms, severity, and detectability of these failures is essential for predicting and preventing failures in blast furnaces, ensuring their safe and efficient operation."
